_about: THE ONE SETTINGS FILE (owner, 16 Nov: single source of truth): values the site and the backend must agree on. tools/cards-gen.js --write copies it as SHARED_SETTINGS into js/core.js and backend/constants.gs; edit here, never there. Never an id, a secret or anybody's data.

roles._about: THE ROLES (owner, 17 Nov), one place: `ids` in order of precedence (the first a person holds is their main role) — each its label, the old words that mean it (`aliases`), what the app calls it (`app`), its rank (people.gs rankOf; a `pending` tutor keeps their other rank), the permission tier its rank maps to (actions.json `roles`), whether a person may tick it for themselves (`self`), and `signIn: false` for a role that never signs in (a contact, owner 17 Nov: a person with no account, never listed, who may have facts; authWhoIs_ gives such a row no token). `default` is a blank role cell; `guest` is nobody signed in. `titles` decide nothing. `tiers` and `ranks` are each in order, lowest first. `notify`: the roles an email reaches somebody by (constants.gs NOTIFY_ALL_ROLES). `form`: the roles the admin's people form ticks, in the order it draws them (people.gs PEOPLE_ROLES_).

may._about: ONE ROLE CHECK (owner, 21 Nov): the fixed words the site's `may_` and the backend's `whoMay_` answer before permissions.json's action rows, both by the shared `mayWord_` (data/settings/roles.js). Each holds when the viewer's tier is in `tiers`, or is not in `notTiers`, or their rank is at least `rank`; `owner` also wants the one owner. Any other word is a permissions.json row.

see._about: THE FOUR SEE ROLES (93, 4h): permissions.json's `see` rows are by these; `words` is the role word (after aliases) each comes from. The site's `seeRoles_` reads it.

limits._about: LIMITS BOTH SIDES KEEP (owner, 20 Nov): how many photos, jobs and library cards a profile holds, favourite links and their title and address lengths, and the weekly email's word cap. Backend constants read these; the site reads SHARED_SETTINGS.limits.

siteRules._about: THE RULES' IDS (496; owner, 20 Nov): every id js/rules.js registers, and those `locked` (never universal, each with its `lock` reason in rules.js). The backend's RULE_IDS and RULES_LOCKED read this; tools/shared-lists.js holds js/rules.js to it.

calendar._about: THE SCHOOL CALENDAR (owner, 17 Nov): each break in its order through the year, the name the site says, the name the terms tab uses, its kind (`half` or `holiday`) and its usual London start (MM-DD); the exams with their config key and usual start. tdYear_ dates the breaks by rule; config `holiday_starts` and `exam_*_start` override the starts.

levels._about: THE LIBRARY'S LEVELS, ONE TABLE (R4; owner, 17 Nov): each level, its rung on the ladder a range is read along (0: never in a range), its key stages, its tiers and its other spellings. A key stage follows from its level, so Find never asks one a level already answers. KS1 SATs and KS2 SATs are two facts and the level is one of them; ESL is off the school ladder, its CEFR bands its tiers. Every level stands on the ladder, by its rung or a key stage (Functional Skills L2 is KS4, so it sorts beside GCSE and a KS4 filter holds it), unless it says `ladder: false` (a level outside England's school years); tools/one-list.js fails one that does neither. LEVEL_TABLE (js/find-aloud.js), the backend's digest and tools/lib/library-schema.js all read this.

quals._about: A QUALIFICATION'S LEVEL (owner, 18 Nov): always one of `list`, which is in order, highest first — a person's qualifications are sorted by it, so the most important never fall off. A stored spelling in `says`, or any library level's `says` above, is read as its canonical name by qualLevel_ (js/data.js), on the site and the server alike. The qualification form offers `list`.
